# Visible Layout Test

Run a visual layout audit of the current Asset Calendar implementation. This is a
verification skill: report evidence and failures; do not silently change source
code or mark a skipped route as passing.

## Scope and guardrails

- Read [the product feature split](../../../docs/proposed-feature-split.md) first.
  Use it to understand the intended shell, responsive boundaries, route ownership,
  role restrictions, and which workflows are implemented. Do not test planned
  routes that are absent from the current route tree as though they existed.
- This repository uses TanStack Router. Treat `src/routeTree.gen.ts`, generated by
  the TanStack Router Vite plugin, as the route manifest after validating it against
  `src/routes/`. Never edit the generated route tree by hand.
- Test only a local URL. The default tenant-aware local URL is
  `http://tenant.localhost:5173`; honor an explicit `LAYOUT_TEST_BASE_URL` only when
  its host is local or a test host. Refuse production hosts, especially
  `nejsumlab.frontend-freelance.dk`.
- The frontend and PocketBase must already be running. Prefer the repository's
  `npm run dev:all`/`vp run dev:all` setup. Do not start a second server, reset
  data, or use production credentials from this skill.
- Use Playwright through the available browser automation tool when possible. If a
  CLI runner is already provided by the environment, it may be used, but do not
  add Playwright to `package.json` as part of an audit.
- Use temporary evidence outside the repository or an existing ignored local
  directory. Do not commit screenshots, cookies, auth state, or test data.

## Audit discipline

- Treat each route, viewport, zoom, DPR, role, and interaction state as an
  independent case. Navigate or reset to a known URL, set the requested browser
  state, reset `scrollX` and `scrollY`, and wait for loading, layout, and fonts to
  settle before measuring.
- Verify the state from inside the page immediately before capture. Record
  `location.href`, `innerWidth`, `innerHeight`, `devicePixelRatio`,
  `visualViewport?.scale`, `scrollX`, `scrollY`, and the root client/scroll
  dimensions. Do not infer the viewport or zoom from a screenshot or browser
  chrome.
- Pair every screenshot with a fresh geometry snapshot from the same settled
  state. The screenshot must be a page capture rather than a browser-window crop;
  if its dimensions do not match the recorded CSS viewport within one pixel,
  mark the visual evidence as mismatched and do not claim a pass from it.
- A tool timeout, empty result, stale page snapshot, or failed browser action is
  not validation. Re-read the current URL and page state with a small focused
  probe before continuing; record the case as `blocked` when the requested state
  cannot be established.
- Never declare a pass from one clean metric. A clean `scrollWidth`, box
  intersection check, or accessibility tree does not override a screenshot that
  shows clipping, edge contact, distortion, crowding, or unreadable text.
- If visual evidence shows a defect that the current probe does not explain,
  stop the pass decision and add a targeted measurement for that symptom:
  rendered text ranges and parent padding for edge contact, adjacent box gaps for
  crowding, intrinsic and rendered ratios for distortion, and viewport/document
  coordinates for clipping. Re-run that focused probe before reporting.
- Restore browser zoom, DPR, media settings, temporary DOM mutations, and test
  data after each case. A later case must not inherit state from an earlier one.

## Procedure

### 1. Read the implementation contract

Read the feature split and then inspect the local routing surface:

1. Read `docs/proposed-feature-split.md` and note the current feature/status
   sections relevant to routes and responsive behavior.
2. Read `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/router.tsx`, and
   `src/routeTree.gen.ts`. Confirm the dev origin and that the TanStack Router
   plugin owns route-tree generation.
3. Run `npm run build` before browser work so the TanStack Router Vite plugin
   builds/regenerates and validates the route tree, then run `npm run check` for
   type and lint diagnostics. Do not modify the generated file manually. If the
   local environment cannot build, stop with a build/setup failure rather than
   running an incomplete route audit.
4. Enumerate `FileRoutesByFullPath` from `src/routeTree.gen.ts`, cross-checking
   each entry against `src/routes/`. Normalize index-route trailing slashes and
   retain dynamic route patterns such as `$resourceId`.
5. Classify routes as public, protected, redirect/index, or dynamic. The current
   route tree includes public sign-in/setup/unavailable pages and protected
   calendar and administration pages. The route tree, not the feature document,
   is the source of the routes actually tested.

### 2. Establish safe browser state

Before collecting layout results:

1. Verify `LAYOUT_TEST_BASE_URL` (or the local default) responds and that the
   PocketBase health path is available through the local proxy. If the server is
   unavailable, stop with a setup failure.
2. Visit public routes first. For protected routes, use an existing local,
   non-production session or the repository's local test fixture. If the app
   requires credentials or tenant data that are not available, ask for a safe
   local test account or report the protected routes as blocked; never guess a
   password or use the production browser page.
3. Use administrator and regular-user local sessions when role-aware navigation
   differs. Verify that protected routes redirect as designed and record the final
   URL after redirects.
4. Resolve dynamic route parameters from real local UI links or temporary local
   records created through the app's existing workflow. Clean up temporary data
   when the app supports it. A dynamic route with no safe local record is
   `blocked`, not `pass`.
5. Create a fresh page/context or clear cookies between role runs. Do not let one
   route's open drawer, scroll position, modal, or cached data contaminate another.

### 3. Build the route/viewport matrix

Visit every current route, including public, protected, index/redirect, and
materialized dynamic routes. For each route, test direct navigation and, where
possible, the in-app link that reaches it. Follow redirects and record both the
requested and final paths.

Do not form a Cartesian product of every route, width, height, DPR, and media
mode. Use these coverage tiers instead:

- Every route: `320x640`, `768x800`, and `1440x900` at the default DPR and media
  settings.
- Routes with mobile navigation or a horizontal composition: add `390x844` and
  `844x390`.
- Routes with fixed/sticky content, dialogs, sheets, or long content: add
  `320x240` and `1440x1440`.
- One representative route for each surface type (public page, authenticated
  shell, list, form, calendar, and dialog when present): add DPR `2` and the
  applicable accessibility, viewport, and font-loading profiles.
- For every responsive breakpoint used by the exercised surface, add a boundary
  pass at one CSS pixel below, exactly at, and one CSS pixel above the breakpoint.
  A layout that passes at `767px` can still fail when a `48rem` media query
  switches at `768px`.

Run basic geometry and overflow checks on every route in the first tier. Run
route-specific states and stress probes only where the route exposes the
corresponding surface. Record `not applicable` with a reason; do not multiply
unrelated profiles across every route.

### 4. Capture baseline geometry

After each navigation, wait for the route's visible content to settle, wait for
`document.fonts.ready` where supported, and allow at least two animation frames
after the last layout-affecting change. Capture a screenshot and a structured
snapshot containing URL, viewport, DPR, visual viewport scale, scroll offsets,
root client/scroll dimensions, visible landmarks, and bounding boxes for
headings, navigation, forms, dialogs, buttons, tables, images, SVGs, and primary
content containers.

Review the screenshot as evidence, not decoration. Check the visual viewport
edges, parent padding and borders, gaps between neighboring controls, shape of
avatars/icons/media, clipped lower content, and whether labels end abruptly.
Compare each visual observation with the geometry snapshot. When browser chrome,
image cropping, or a tool screenshot makes the viewport ambiguous, capture a
fresh page-only screenshot and mark the ambiguous capture unsupported until it
matches the measured CSS viewport.

Use a 1 CSS-pixel tolerance for arithmetic checks. Flag a failure when:

- The document or its scrolling element has any page-level scrolling
  (`scrollWidth > clientWidth` or `scrollHeight > clientHeight`). The complete
  page must remain fixed in both directions; only a documented internal scroller
  may scroll, and it must not cause the document root to scroll.
- A visible control, label, focus indicator, or required content is outside the
  visual viewport, clipped, overlapped, or unreachable at the tested state.
- A visible interactive control or required content crosses either visual
  viewport edge at the initial scroll position. Measure its viewport-relative
  `getBoundingClientRect()` and report the off-screen pixels, even when the
  document technically exposes a horizontal scrollbar. A right-edge action that
  is only reachable by horizontal page scrolling is a failure, not a passing
  responsive layout.
- Any visible repeated item, list row, card, table row, or required descendant
  extends below or beyond the visual viewport at the initial scroll position,
  unless it is wholly owned by an intentional internal scroller. A list whose
  lower content is cut off by the viewport or a clipping ancestor is a failure
  even when the list itself reports no scrollable overflow.
- Two unrelated visible boxes intersect. Exclude intentional containment such as
  an icon inside a button and a modal scrim behind its dialog.
- An unrelated landmark moves during a state transition beyond the measured
  expected change. Capture geometry before, during, and after the transition.
- Text is clipped, wraps into an unusable control, or causes a control to resize
  unpredictably.
- A visible asset, avatar, initials badge, icon, media element, or fixed-size
  control is distorted by sizing or flex/grid shrink. Compare its rendered
  width and height with its intrinsic ratio, declared `aspect-ratio`, equal
  width/height contract, and minimum dimensions. A circular or square element
  that renders as an ellipse or a compressed icon is a failure even when it is
  fully inside the viewport.
- Two unrelated visible regions or interactive targets are crowded together.
  Measure the visual gap between adjacent boxes that share an edge axis; flag a
  zero or negative gap, and flag a gap below `4px` when the elements are
  separate shell regions, controls, actions, or landmarks. Do not flag children
  inside the same button, or controls in the same-row documented segmented
  control with a shared visual treatment. A shared DOM parent is not enough to
  exempt stacked controls with different actions, such as navigation buttons
  followed by a separate Today action. A layout can fail this check without any
  box intersection or overflow.
- Text is pressed against, clipped by, or allowed to paint through its parent
  edge without a readable layout contract. Measure the rendered line boxes
  against the parent's border and padding box; flag less than `4px` of visible
  edge clearance for bordered or filled containers, or less than `8px` for
  interactive controls, unless the surface is explicitly edge-to-edge.
- A constrained text run is clipped with `overflow: hidden`, `overflow: clip`,
  or `white-space: nowrap` without verified `text-overflow: ellipsis`, a
  readable reflow, or an accessible disclosure containing the full value. Do
  not accept `text-overflow: clip` merely because the element's own
  `scrollWidth` is clean; inspect rendered ranges and the parent box.

Also flag content that is technically visible but unusable because a flexible
column becomes too narrow. A long label is not passing merely because
`overflow-wrap: anywhere` prevents horizontal overflow. Inspect the rendered
text range and its containing block, including inline descendants such as
`strong`, `span`, and links whose own `clientWidth` or `scrollWidth` may be zero.
Flag a repeated item when any of the following is true:

- A meaningful label wraps to three or more lines, or its average line length
  is three characters or fewer, because fixed siblings consume the row width.
- A label or value column is narrower than `8ch` while its row contains usable
  sibling actions or metadata that could be laid out below it.
- One repeated row is more than twice the median height of its siblings solely
  because its text wraps, or its action/metadata columns are vertically
  misaligned with the associated label.
- A long value forces a sibling control, status, or action into an unusably
  narrow column even when no boxes intersect and `scrollWidth` is clean.

Use `Range.getClientRects()` or an equivalent rendered-line measurement for
inline text. Record the text, selector, line count, text box, containing row
box, sibling boxes, and the screenshot. Prefer a stacked or intentionally
truncated layout that preserves readable labels and reachable actions. Do not
silence this finding with `overflow: hidden` unless the full value remains
available through an accessible disclosure.

`getBoundingClientRect()` is necessary but not sufficient. Also inspect scroll
containers, scroll offsets, computed transforms, and screenshots. Evaluate both
viewport coordinates and document coordinates so nested scrolling and portals do
not hide a collision.

For every horizontal overflow failure, identify the smallest offending element
whose right or left edge exceeds the visual viewport, then walk its ancestor
chain to the first element where `scrollWidth > clientWidth`. Record the
offending element, its visible and document-relative boxes, the ancestor's
scroll dimensions and computed overflow, and whether the overflow is page-level
or an intentional accessible scroller. Repeat the check after focusing the
rightmost visible controls; focus must not leave the control partially or wholly
outside the viewport.

Apply the same procedure vertically. Inspect the document scrolling element,
`html`, and `body` for `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, then locate the lowest
visible content box whose bottom exceeds `innerHeight`. Report the selector,
off-screen pixels, clipping ancestor, and whether the content is a list item,
action, footer, or other required landmark. Do not treat a screenshot that ends
before the final repeated item as a pass. If an internal scroller is intentional,
verify that it is the only scrolling surface, that every item can be reached with
keyboard and pointer scrolling, and that the root page remains fixed.

For distortion checks, inventory visible `img`, `svg`, `canvas`, `video`, avatar,
badge, icon, initials, and fixed-size control elements. Measure their rendered
box and compare it with the strongest available contract, in this order:
intrinsic media ratio, explicit `aspect-ratio`, equal declared width and height,
or declared `min-width` and `min-height`. Flag a ratio difference greater than
5% or a shrink below a declared fixed dimension, unless the element explicitly
uses an intentional crop or responsive transform such as `object-fit: cover`.
For flex and grid descendants, also record `flex-shrink`, computed minimum sizes,
and the sibling content that caused compression. Verify that `preserveAspectRatio`
and equivalent media behavior remain intact. Capture the distorted element and
its containing control in the evidence screenshot.

For spacing checks, inspect direct children and actionable descendants of
headers, navigation bars, toolbars, form action rows, cards, list rows, and other
repeated layout regions. Sort visible boxes by the relevant axis and calculate
the gap between adjacent boxes whose projections overlap on the perpendicular
axis. Report the pair when the gap is below the threshold, including each
selector, both boxes, the parent layout mode, computed `gap`, margins, padding,
action semantics, and whether the pair belongs to an intentional same-row
grouped-control exception. A contiguous exception applies only when the
controls are documented as one same-row group; it does not excuse a stacked
control row or controls with different actions. Repeat after long-content, zoom,
font scaling, and responsive-breakpoint probes because sibling compression can
remove otherwise valid spacing.

For text edge checks, inspect text-bearing descendants of buttons, links, inputs,
cards, list rows, navigation items, and other bordered or filled containers.
Measure `Range.getClientRects()` for the rendered text, then compare every line's
left and right edges with the containing block's border and padding edges. Record
computed padding, `overflow`, `white-space`, and `text-overflow`. When the text
reaches or crosses the content edge, determine whether it reflows, truncates with
an actual ellipsis, or exposes the complete value through an accessible name,
tooltip, disclosure, or equivalent. A long unbroken resource or user name is a
required probe value, not an exception.

## Required stress families

### 5. Grid and flex intrinsic sizing

Inspect flexible grid and flex descendants on every route. Temporarily test
representative content only in containers that use those layout modes, restoring
the DOM after each probe:

- Very wide intrinsic children and `white-space: nowrap` text.
- Unconstrained images, SVGs with intrinsic widths, long URLs, `<pre>`, code
  blocks, and wide tables.
- Long sibling labels beside avatars, initials, icons, badges, and fixed-size
  controls; verify that the shape-dependent element keeps its intended ratio
  and minimum dimensions while the text yields or reflows.
- Adjacent shell regions, navigation items, toolbar actions, and form controls;
  verify that unrelated targets retain visible separation instead of becoming
  edge-to-edge through flex/grid compression.
- Stacked controls with different actions, including navigation plus Today or
  primary plus secondary actions; verify that rows do not touch unless the
  product explicitly documents a compact grouped treatment.
- Long unbroken labels inside constrained buttons, links, navigation items, and
  cards; verify readable right and left insets and an explicit reflow,
  ellipsis, or accessible disclosure instead of text ending at the parent edge.
- `grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr` and grid tracks whose min-content size can
  exceed the container.
- Flex children whose computed `min-width` is `auto`, including nested flex
  containers.

A flexible child that can shrink must have `min-width: 0` or an equivalent
intentional sizing/overflow rule. Flag cases where a long descendant expands a
flex/grid track, pushes siblings out of view, or creates page-level scrolling.
Do not accept `overflow: hidden` as a fix when it makes content inaccessible;
intentional scrollers must expose their scroll direction and remain keyboard
accessible.

### 5a. Content density and adversarial data

Exercise each repeated list, directory, card, and row with the longest safe
local labels, email addresses, statuses, URLs, and action text already present
in local data. When the route has no sufficiently long local value, temporarily
replace a rendered text node with representative long content and restore the
DOM immediately after the probe. Test both the narrow responsive layout and
the nearest desktop layout. Compare repeated-item heights and rendered text
line boxes before declaring the surface usable.

### 6. Overflow propagation

For every visible target and its ancestors up to the document root, inspect
computed `overflow`, `overflow-x`, `overflow-y`, `overflow: clip`, `contain`, and
`contain: paint`. Report an ancestor that clips rendered content, focus rings,
menus, tooltips, or dialogs unexpectedly.

At every tested viewport, explicitly record `document.scrollingElement`,
`document.documentElement`, and `document.body` client and scroll dimensions.
Fail the route when either axis scrolls at the page level. Also compare every
repeated item's viewport box with `0 <= top` and `bottom <= innerHeight` at the
initial scroll position; this catches lower list content that is visually cut off
without creating a separate list scrollbar.

Exercise intentional `overflow: auto` containers for:

- Nested horizontal and vertical scroll traps.
- Scrollbar appearance changing available width and causing a layout shift.
- Simultaneous horizontal/vertical scrolling.
- Focused elements that are clipped rather than scrolled into view.
- Keyboard scrolling with `Tab`, arrow keys, `PageDown`, `Home`, and `End`.

Check both the document and each scrollable ancestor; a clean document
`scrollWidth` does not prove that intermediate content is reachable.

### 7. Height stress testing

Run the short and very tall height checks only for routes identified as
height-sensitive in the matrix. Verify that fixed headers do not consume all
usable space, sticky content does not cover the active content, bottom sheets do
not cover controls, modals fit vertically or scroll internally, primary actions
remain reachable, and footers do not overlap or trap content.

Open every available dialog, drawer, popover, form, and confirmation surface at
the shortest supported heights. Scroll the surface and verify the focused action
remains visible.

### 8. Fixed, sticky, absolute, and transformed positioning

Inventory visible elements with `position: fixed`, `sticky`, or `absolute`, and
ancestors with `transform`, `scale`, `translate`, negative margins, or
containment that creates a new containing block. Test them at the top, middle,
and bottom of the document and inside nested scrollers.

Check collisions in visual viewport coordinates and document coordinates. Include
portaled menus/dialogs and transformed elements in the screenshot review. A
bounding box that looks valid before scrolling is not enough if the element is
clipped or overlaps after an ancestor scrolls.

### 9. Modern viewport behavior

Test portrait and landscape, short and very tall viewports, and mobile-sized
pages with the available mobile Playwright context. Inspect usage of `100vh`,
`100svh`, `100lvh`, `100dvh`, and `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Focus an input and
reduce the viewport to simulate virtual-keyboard pressure; verify the focused
field and submit action remain reachable.

Exercise viewport changes that represent browser chrome expansion/collapse. Use
safe-area/notch emulation when supported. Test 100% browser zoom separately from
CSS `html { font-size: ... }` changes; do not claim a font-size override is
browser-zoom coverage. Repeat at unusual DPRs and record unsupported emulation
as a limitation.

### 10. Accessibility modes beyond 200% font scaling

Run 200%, 300%, and 400% effective text scaling, browser zoom, and a temporary
root font-size change on the representative surface routes. Use the baseline
route pass to detect which additional routes need a focused reflow rerun.

Use the integrated browser's real zoom control or zoom command for browser-zoom
passes when it is available. Browser zoom is not the same as DPR, CSS
`transform: scale`, CSS `zoom`, or a larger root font size. After applying each
zoom level, verify and record `window.devicePixelRatio`,
`window.visualViewport?.scale`, `innerWidth`, `innerHeight`, and the root client
and scroll dimensions. If the requested zoom cannot be applied or verified,
record it as unsupported rather than simulating a pass and calling it browser
zoom. Restore 100% browser zoom before the next independent profile.

Run DPR separately by creating a browser context with the requested
`deviceScaleFactor` while keeping the CSS viewport constant. Record the same
metrics and do not classify a DPR-only pass as browser-zoom coverage. At each
verified zoom and DPR combination, rerun root scrolling, viewport clipping,
fixed-size distortion, text wrapping, and focused-control reachability checks.

Also exercise:

- `forced-colors: active` / Windows High Contrast emulation.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast` media settings.
- Large system-font-like metrics, increased line height, letter spacing, and word
  spacing.
- Keyboard-only navigation with visible `:focus`/`:focus-visible` indicators.
- Accessible names and roles using Playwright's accessibility snapshot facilities
  where available; do not make hidden diagnostic labels visible in the app.
- Focus indicators entirely inside the viewport and minimum touch targets of
  44x44 CSS pixels unless the product contract documents another target.

### 11. Interaction and state-transition stress

For every route that exposes them, exercise focus and focus-visible states,
keyboard navigation, menus, dialogs, accordions, popovers, tooltips,
expanded/collapsed regions, validation error/warning/success states, disabled and
loading states, selected/checked/pressed/dragged states, skeleton-to-content
changes, and toast/notification entry and removal.

Use safe local data and avoid destructive actions unless the test can restore the
state. Capture geometry before, during, and after each transition. Assert that
unrelated landmarks do not move unexpectedly, the active/focused control remains
visible, and closing a surface restores focus and scroll position according to
its route contract. Run a rapid open/close or repeated transition pass to expose
race-condition layout shifts.

### 12. Font loading states

Test representative surface routes with fonts blocked or failed so fallback
metrics are visible, then with normal webfont loading, and finally with
deliberately delayed font loading. Repeat on any route whose baseline geometry
shows font-dependent overflow.
Where the app uses variable fonts, exercise its supported weight/axis values and
at least one weight change.

Check `font-display: swap` and `optional` behavior where present. Wait for
`document.fonts.ready` before the loaded capture, and compare fallback, loading,
and loaded geometry. Flag either direction of failure: content that overflows
before the webfont arrives or content that overflows only after it replaces the
fallback. Restore routing/font mocks after each state.

## Reporting and completion

Produce a compact report with:

- Local base URL, commit/worktree state if available, browser engine, and the
  viewport/DPR/media matrix actually run.
- Every route with `pass`, `fail`, `blocked`, or `not applicable`; include the
  requested path and final path after redirects.
- Failures grouped by category, route, viewport, state, and the smallest useful
  selector/ancestor chain. Include the measured boxes, scroll dimensions, and a
  screenshot for visual failures when the runner supports it.
- For each failure, include one evidence bundle from the same settled state:
  requested and verified browser settings, URL, geometry measurements, the
  smallest selector chain, and the matching screenshot. Never combine a
  screenshot from one viewport or scroll position with measurements from
  another.
- Include a `page-level scroll/clipped content` category for any root vertical or
  horizontal scroll, or any required list/card content outside the viewport.
  Report both axes, root client/scroll dimensions, off-screen pixels, and the
  smallest offending selector/ancestor chain.
- Include an `unusable wrapping/content density` category for readable-but-
  unusable text. Report the rendered line count, text and row boxes, sibling
  boxes, median repeated-row height, and the smallest useful selector chain;
  do not report this only as a generic overflow or intrinsic-sizing failure.
- Include a `visual distortion/aspect-ratio` category for compressed or
  stretched content. Report the selector, measured width and height, expected
  ratio or minimum size, shrink/computed sizing properties, and the sibling
  content that caused the distortion.
- Include a `crowded adjacency/spacing` category for unrelated boxes whose
  visual gap is below the threshold. Report both selectors and boxes, measured
  gap, parent layout properties, and why the pair is not an intentional grouped
  control.
- Include a `text edge clearance/truncation` category for text that reaches a
  parent edge or is clipped without a readable contract. Report the text
  selector, rendered line boxes, parent box, edge clearance, computed padding and
  overflow properties, and whether reflow, ellipsis, or accessible disclosure
  was expected.
- Blocked routes and unsupported browser emulations separately from passes.
- State any evidence mismatch, unavailable zoom/DPR emulation, stale or failed
  browser action, and skipped focused probe separately from route passes.
- A short list of likely fixes, especially whether the failure requires
  `min-width: 0`, an intentional scroll container, changed viewport-unit usage,
  focus management, or a stacking/containing-block adjustment.

The audit is complete only when every route in the current generated route tree
has a recorded result, every applicable stress family has run, and any blocked or
unsupported coverage is explicit. A clean document overflow check alone is not a
passing layout audit.
